editorial:
Imagine living in a gray, concrete skyscraper where everything feels a bit dull. That is exactly how life is for a twelve-year-old boy dealing with divorced parents. Luckily, his world gets a lot brighter because he lives right next to a horse farm and a racing track. He forms a special bond with Evergreen, a former champion horse who has seen better days. When the people running the farm decide the old horse is useless and plan to send him to a slaughterhouse, the boy and his friends refuse to let that happen. It creates a heartfelt vibe that reminds you of those classic stories about kids fighting for what is right.

You will love how the movie captures the bravery and innocence of childhood. The acting feels natural, and the tension builds up nicely when the kids actually steal the horse to save its life. While some parts move a bit slow, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you are looking for a sweet family flick, you should definitely check this one out. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the vintage cityscapes clearly, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night with your kids.
endingExplained: After stealing Evergreen to save him from the slaughterhouse, the kids realize that they cannot keep a horse hidden in a big city forever. Instead of giving up, they find a way to make the horse a permanent part of their community. They end up giving Evergreen as a gift to the boy's entire class. This selfless act saves the horse's life and brings the students together, giving the horse a happy new home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about animals and friendship.
